reviews.review: Great fast paced action shooter with unmatched replay-ability and surprisingly appealing worldbuilding. While the narrative ending may not be exactly fulfilling, the rest of the game easily makes up of it. It offers an amazingly wide range of builds, allowing players to customise their character’s skills and mods to an incredible degree. Where this gem truly shines is playing with friends. I’ve had an amazing time exploring and collecting armor, guns, and items. Truly a labour of love and well worth the investment.

As someone who had never played a soulslike before, I was hesitant to get Remnant when my brother invited me. He explained that it was the sequel to RFTA, which I had never even heard of. Despite that, I was craving a coop experience and felt that this could be the game that would scratch that itch, and so I bit the bullet and started playing. Immediately, it became clear to me that this game was special, not just in its atmosphere and level design, but also in the gunplay that felt so remarkably fine-tuned that I genuinely would've believed if this game were an AAA title. There is a certain feeling of excitement that washes over you everytime you enter a new dungeon, boss arena, or world. No playthrough is ever the same, and even if you encounter the same world boss, you'll be delighted to know that there are so many alternate fights you can engage which will lead you to an entirely different fight. It's like a new game all over again, with unexpected mazes, puzzles, secrets, and new enemy designs. It's crazy to think that a studio of this caliber was able to pump out such a high quality game that doesn't reuse assets, enemies, or movesets, and instead introduces wholly new enemy types and attacks. I'm writing this review now after all DLCs have come out because I believe that the game is in the best state it's ever been in, with the developers having taken all the community feedback to roll out patches and updates that helped make the game feel even more polished and fun to play. Admittedly, there are those who will not find the same euphoria that this game has brought me. But, having played for over 200 hours, trying every world and dungeon multiple times, and collecting every item in the game, I can confidently say that, at the very least, you should give Remnant 2 a try. I am confident that the refund period will give you enough of an idea to whether or not you will enjoy it. At the end of the day, Remnant 2 is religious experience, and I am so thankful that my brother decided to introduce me to it. I am glad to have been able to enjoy such a masterpiece, with so much build variety that I am confident I will still be hooked a year from now. If you are thinking of getting a game to play with your friends, or just want to try something new, give Remnant 2 a chance and see where the wind takes you.
